key_insight: A physics-constrained neural-network strength function preserves accurate phase-field strength surfaces at regularization lengths up to 10 times the Irwin characteristic length.
engineering_relevance: Decoupling strength accuracy from regularization length reduces mesh-resolution demands for phase-field fracture simulations of large structures.
method: Learn the material strength function directly from data using a physics-constrained neural network.
Calibrate the nucleation driving force against multiple strength states and enforce openness in selected directions.
Embed the learned strength function in phase-field fracture simulations.
evidence_signal: Tests cover four synthetic strength surfaces, experimental data for graphite and two rubbers, and finite-element fracture simulations; learned surfaces remain accurate up to ε = 10 l_ch, while analytic counterparts perform comparatively poorly even at ε = 0.5 l_ch.
watch_item: Reliability beyond the sampled strength states and loading regimes requires validation, particularly when selecting directions in which the strength surface remains open.
paper_title: Machine learning of strength surfaces enables high regularization length phase-field fracture
